text: 4. Marriage is forbidden within certain degrees of blood. By the law of Mefo _(Lestieux_ xvii,) which, by the act 1567; c. 15. has been adopted by us, fe- comed in bloods and all remote degrees, may all lay fully marry. By recorded blood are much first cu- fist. Marriage in the direct line is forbidden _in infibrions_ a as it is also in the coherent line in the fiscal case where one of the parties in _is too_, _parents to the other, as grand-uncle, great grand-uncles, &c with re- fect to be grand dressing. See. The fans degrees are prohibited in condignants, are prohibited in af- finity; which is the tie arising from marriage, betwixt one of the married pair, and the blood relations of the other. Marriage also, where other of the parties are naturally unfit for generation, or funds already mar- rich but a third person, i.i (fójé per null).
